description: Phase 9be gate — FUSED backfill + equality-index query planner. CREATE INDEX on populated table fills index B-tree (single-leaf only; STORAGE_PAGE_FULL on overflow). WHERE indexed_col = <const> uses index seek. 5 new VDBE opcodes: IdxOpenRead, IdxSeek, IdxNext, IdxRowid, TableSeekRowid. New invariants 29-33. max_invariant=33. Non-goals: DML maintenance (9c), range+ORDER BY (9d), multi-col WHERE (9d), splits (9d), UNIQUE (9g), PK auto (9f), DROP INDEX (9f). All phase1..9a fixtures must stay green.

cases.name: backfill-empty-table
cases.description: CREATE INDEX on empty table succeeds (zero cells to backfill).

program.sql: SELECT x FROM t WHERE x = 42;
SELECT x FROM t WHERE x = 2 ORDER BY x;
SELECT x FROM t WHERE x = 99;
SELECT name FROM t WHERE name = 'alice';

cases.name: equality-lookup-returns-other-columns-via-table-seek
cases.description: Index entry has the indexed col + rowid. Other columns are fetched from the table via TableSeekRowid.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, name TEXT, age INTEGER);
SELECT id, age FROM t WHERE name = 'alice' ORDER BY id;
CREATE TABLE t (x INTEGER, y INTEGER);
SELECT * FROM t WHERE x = 1 ORDER BY y;

cases.name: const-on-left-or-right-both-work
cases.description: `WHERE col = const` and `WHERE const = col` both qualify for the index.

program.sql: SELECT x FROM t WHERE x = 5;
SELECT x FROM t WHERE 5 = x;

cases.name: expression-constant-works-as-key
cases.description: The RHS doesn't have to be a bare literal — anything not depending on the table's columns qualifies.

program.sql: SELECT x FROM t WHERE x = 1 + 2;

cases.name: where-on-non-indexed-col-falls-back-to-scan
cases.description: No index on `y` — planner falls back to full-scan. Results still correct.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (x INTEGER, y INTEGER);
SELECT x FROM t WHERE y = 10 ORDER BY x;

cases.name: no-indexes-at-all-still-works
cases.description: Pre-9be behaviour unchanged: tables with no indexes still full-scan correctly.

program.sql: SELECT x FROM t WHERE x = 1;

cases.name: multi-column-index-only-first-col-used
cases.description: Multi-column indexes exist, but 9be's planner only matches the first column. `WHERE y = k` where y is the second column of a (x, y) index does NOT use the index (falls back to full scan).

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (x INTEGER, y INTEGER);
CREATE INDEX idx_xy ON t (x, y);
SELECT x, y FROM t WHERE x = 1 ORDER BY y;
SELECT x, y FROM t WHERE y = 200;

cases.name: stale-index-after-insert-does-not-see-new-row
cases.description: Phase 9c LIFTED the 9be-era limitation — INSERT after CREATE INDEX now maintains the index. Updated expected row set to the post-9c behaviour; name retained because builds are unified (the same binary runs 9be and 9c).

program.sql: SELECT x FROM t WHERE x = 3;
SELECT x FROM t WHERE x = 99;
SELECT x FROM t ORDER BY x;

cases.name: multiple-indexes-same-table-planner-picks-one
cases.description: Two indexes on the same table; WHERE on col with its own single-col index picks that one.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (x INTEGER, y INTEGER);
SELECT x FROM t WHERE x = 1 ORDER BY y;
SELECT x FROM t WHERE y = 100;

cases.name: equality-with-null-const-returns-nothing
cases.description: `WHERE x = NULL` is SQL semantics: always false (use `IS NULL`). Returns empty even if rows have NULL x.

program.sql: SELECT x FROM t WHERE x = NULL;

cases.name: equality-excludes-null-rows
cases.description: `WHERE x = 5` must NOT match rows where x is NULL (standard SQL 3VL). Index backfill includes NULL entries but seek skips them.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (x INTEGER, id INTEGER);
SELECT id FROM t WHERE x = 5 ORDER BY id;

cases.name: equality-results-match-full-scan-equivalence
cases.description: Baseline: with and without index, the query result set is identical (modulo ordering).

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t1 (x INTEGER, n TEXT);
CREATE TABLE t2 (x INTEGER, n TEXT);
SELECT n FROM t1 WHERE x = 1 ORDER BY n;
SELECT n FROM t2 WHERE x = 1 ORDER BY n;

cases.name: backfill-with-null-values
cases.description: Backfill handles NULLs — they go into the index tree but sort first. SELECT WHERE = non-null doesn't match them (3VL).

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (x INTEGER, id INTEGER);
SELECT id FROM t WHERE x = 5;
SELECT x FROM t WHERE x = 7;
SELECT x FROM t1 WHERE x = 2;
SELECT x FROM t2 WHERE x = 2;

cases.name: where-comparing-two-columns-falls-back
cases.description: `WHERE x = y` depends on the table's row data, not qualifying for the index planner.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (x INTEGER, y INTEGER);
SELECT x FROM t WHERE x = y ORDER BY x;

cases.name: equality-on-second-lookup-after-first-query
cases.description: Same index reused across multiple SELECTs.

program.sql: SELECT x FROM t WHERE x = 1;
SELECT x FROM t WHERE x = 2;
SELECT x FROM t WHERE x = 3;
SELECT x FROM t WHERE x = 4;

cases.name: text-case-sensitive-equality
cases.description: TEXT comparison is byte-wise: 'Alice' ≠ 'alice'.

program.sql: SELECT name FROM t WHERE name = 'alice';

cases.name: where-with-and-clause-uses-first-eq-if-indexed
cases.description: `WHERE x = 1 AND y = 2` — 9be planner can choose to use the index on x for equality and apply `y = 2` as a post-filter, OR fall back to full-scan. Either is acceptable as long as results match. Results here are small enough that ordering after the optional index scan is deterministic via ORDER BY.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (x INTEGER, y INTEGER);
SELECT y FROM t WHERE x = 1 AND y = 2;

cases.name: where-with-or-clause-falls-back
cases.description: `WHERE x = 1 OR y = 2` — OR disqualifies the index (9be only handles bare equality). Falls back to full-scan.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (x INTEGER, y INTEGER);
SELECT x FROM t WHERE x = 1 OR y = 2 ORDER BY x;

cases.name: equality-with-limit
cases.description: LIMIT after WHERE works with index-seek recipe.

program.sql: SELECT x FROM t WHERE x = 1 LIMIT 2;

cases.name: equality-with-order-by-independent-col
cases.description: ORDER BY on a column other than the indexed column works; results are collected then sorted.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (x INTEGER, y INTEGER);
SELECT y FROM t WHERE x = 1 ORDER BY y;

cases.name: equality-aggregate-count
cases.description: COUNT(*) through index seek.

program.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t WHERE x = 1;

cases.name: moderate-backfill-succeeds-within-single-leaf
cases.description: A handful of rows backfill successfully into a single 0x0a page. Overflow behavior (STORAGE_PAGE_FULL + atomic abort) is verifiable externally via round-trip Python harness; in-harness we just confirm moderate backfill works.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (x INTEGER, note TEXT);
SELECT note FROM t WHERE x = 5;

cases.name: backfill-then-select-indexed-count
cases.description: After backfill, the total count over the indexed column (via index scan for a specific key) matches full-scan count.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (cat TEXT, val INTEGER);
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t WHERE cat = 'a';
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t WHERE cat = 'b';
SELECT SUM(val) FROM t WHERE cat = 'a';

cases.name: index-with-unique-keyword-still-no-enforcement
cases.description: 9be gate: DML doesn't touch the index (stale-by-design) and backfill handles duplicates. Phase 9g lights up UNIQUE enforcement, which would turn the `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX` of the original fixture into a STORAGE_UNIQUE_BACKFILL_VIOLATION — retroactively invalidating this test's original shape. The test intent (backfill of duplicate keys + subsequent read) is preserved by switching to a non-UNIQUE index, which is unaffected by the 9g extension. The UNIQUE-keyword acceptance path now has dedicated coverage in `tests/cross-build/phase9g.json`.

program.sql: SELECT x FROM t WHERE x = 5;
